questions.prompt: A continuous random variable $X$ follows the normal distribution $X \sim \text{N}(50, 4^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the standard scores $z_a$ and $z_b$ corresponding to the interval boundaries $x = 46$ and $x = 58$.

questions.prompt: Let $Z \sim \text{N}(0, 1)$ denote the standard normal variable.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Using the standard normal distribution table, find $P(0.5 < Z < 1.5)$.

questions.prompt: A normal variable $X$ has mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Using the central area formula $2\Phi(k) - 1$, find the probability $P(\mu - 1.2\sigma < X < \mu + 1.2\sigma)$.

questions.prompt: The random variable $Z$ has the standard normal distribution $Z \sim \text{N}(0, 1)$.
Two normal models $X_1 \sim \text{N}(100, 10^2)$ and $X_2 \sim \text{N}(100, 20^2)$ have the same mean but different standard deviations.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: State which distribution has the greater probability of lying in the interval $90 < X < 110$, and explain why without full calculation.

questions.prompt: Let $Z \sim \text{N}(0, 1)$ denote the standard normal variable.
The running times $T$ minutes of participants in a $10\text{ km}$ race are normally distributed with mean 55 minutes and standard deviation 6 minutes, so that $T \sim \text{N}(55, 6^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen participant finishes the race in between 49 and 61 minutes.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen participant finishes the race in between 58 and 64 minutes.

questions.prompt: The mass $W$ grams of breakfast cereal in a standard box follows the normal distribution $W \sim \text{N}(500, 12^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen box has mass between 482 g and 500 g.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A random sample of 400 boxes is inspected. Find the expected number of boxes in the sample with mass between 482 g and 518 g.

questions.prompt: The volume $V$ ml of drink dispensed into bottles by a machine is normally distributed with mean $750\text{ ml}$ and standard deviation $8\text{ ml}$, so that $V \sim \text{N}(750, 8^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that a randomly chosen bottle contains between $738\text{ ml}$ and $746\text{ ml}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A bottle is rejected by quality control if its volume lies outside the interval $734\text{ ml}$ to $766\text{ ml}$. Find the probability that a randomly chosen bottle is rejected.

questions.prompt: The daily revenue $S$ thousand dollars of a supermarket branch is modeled by $S \sim \text{N}(24.0, 3.5^2)$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the probability that on a randomly chosen day, the revenue is between 19.1 thousand dollars and 28.2 thousand dollars.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: In a trading year of 250 operating days, find the expected number of days on which revenue exceeds 29.6 thousand dollars.

questions.prompt: A continuous random variable $Y$ follows a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find $P(\mu - 0.75\sigma < Y < \mu + 0.75\sigma)$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the probability that $Y$ lies within $1.6$ standard deviations of its mean, and hence state the probability that $Y$ differs from its mean by more than $1.6$ standard deviations.

questions.prompt: A manufacturer produces steel ball bearings whose diameters $D\text{ mm}$ follow $D \sim \text{N}(15.00, 0.08^2)$. Bearings are accepted for commercial use if their diameters satisfy $14.86\text{ mm} \le D \le 15.14\text{ mm}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the probability that a randomly chosen ball bearing is accepted is $0.9198$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Accepted bearings are further graded as Premium if their diameters lie in the tighter interval $14.92\text{ mm} \le D \le 15.08\text{ mm}$. Calculate the probability that a randomly chosen bearing is graded as Premium.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Given that a randomly chosen ball bearing is accepted, find the conditional probability that it is graded as Premium, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt:
Two automated machines, Alpha and Beta, produce metal washers with nominal diameter $25.0\text{ mm}$. The actual diameters follow independent normal distributions:
- Machine Alpha: $X_A \sim \text{N}(25.0, 0.4^2)$
- Machine Beta: $X_B \sim \text{N}(25.0, 0.5^2)$
A washer is within specification if its diameter lies between $24.4\text{ mm}$ and $25.6\text{ mm}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate the probability that a washer produced by Machine Alpha is within specification.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the probability that a washer produced by Machine Beta is within specification, and explain without calculation why this probability is less than that for Machine Alpha.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: A random sample of 5 washers is selected independently from Machine Alpha. Find the probability that at least 4 of the washers in the sample are within specification, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
